episode_title: Episode 284: How AI Is Changing the Way We Do Business with Matt McKenzie

real_qa.q: What was Alloy Digital's most notable project and how did it impact Toyota North America's lead generation?
real_qa.r: Alloy Digital conceived and launched the original version of buyatoyota.com, which became Toyota North America's number one lead generation platform for approximately 15 years, among many other solutions delivered to large enterprise-scale companies.
real_qa.requete: buyatoyota.com Alloy Digital Toyota lead generation

real_qa.q: What is Meaningful AI's core philosophy on how artificial intelligence should impact human jobs and capabilities?
real_qa.r: Meaningful AI's core tenet is humanity—the view that AI has the opportunity to remove monotonous non-human tasks like copying and pasting, freeing people to focus on human judgment where AI as a probabilistic model is not good. Rather than eliminating jobs, AI should enhance human capabilities and empower people, with humans needing to monitor, create judgment around, and act on AI-generated information.
real_qa.requete: Meaningful AI humanity core philosophy job impact

real_qa.q: What percentage of small organizations with fewer than 50 employees view AI as an unsuitable solution?
real_qa.r: Organizations with fewer than 50 people, approximately 86% felt that AI was not a good solution for them, reflecting both fear and misunderstanding of AI's potential for small business benefit.

real_qa.q: How did Matt McKenzie transition from technology engineering into entrepreneurship and business development at Alloy Digital?
real_qa.r: After graduating from Vanderbilt, McKenzie took a job supporting the university's IT infrastructure, which gave him real-world experience. When he later worked at a company in Tuscaloosa, he pitched a product idea, was allowed to build it, and then was sent to sell it directly to major companies like Reynolds, Rubbermaid, Tyco, and Alcoa—this sales experience taught him the critical difference between building what engineers think is needed versus what customers actually want, launching his entrepreneurial journey.
real_qa.requete: Alloy Digital entrepreneurship business development sales

real_qa.q: What is the fundamental principle McKenzie advises entrepreneurs to follow before launching a company?
real_qa.r: McKenzie advises entrepreneurs to never start a company without starting with a client first, partnering with that client to determine what actually fits their needs. By demonstrating market traction—showing that at least one real company will pay for your solution—you prove you are solving a genuine problem, creating a foundation to build a sustainable business around.
real_qa.requete: start company first client McKenzie advice

guest.bio_context: Matt McKenzie grew up on a farm in Alabama and became a technologist from childhood, earning a bachelor's degree from Vanderbilt University where he initially pursued engineering before switching to economics. He worked in systems administration, cybersecurity, and software development before co-founding Alloy Digital in August 2015, which he ran for over 15 years while managing projects for major enterprise clients including Toyota North America. He co-founded Deploy with Chase Morrow to support talent in the technology ecosystem, and in August 2023 launched Meaningful AI to help organizations and people advance through AI adoption.
